course_name_original: Engineering of high-voltage transmission and distribution systems
course_name_en: Engineering of high-voltage transmission and distribution systems

learning_outcomes.text: Has a theoretically well-founded knowledge of the design and operation of high-voltage transmission and distribution systems for electrical energy.
Is able to combine knowledge of the structure and technologies of materials with their application in modern electrical engineering designs.
Is able to obtain information from literature, databases, and other sources; is able to integrate acquired information, interpret it, draw conclusions, and formulate and justify opinions.
Understands the need and knows the possibilities of continuous self-education and raising one's professional competences.

syllabus_topics: Operation of transmission and distribution systems in the power system (1 hour). Technical and economic characteristics. Conditions for transmitting large powers via overhead and cable lines. Requirements for the selection of insulation systems.

Operational stresses of overhead insulation systems (2 hours). Operational stresses of insulators in power lines and substations. Design and electrical parameters of insulators. Mechanism of pollution flashover. Pollution zones. Selection of insulators for pollution conditions.

Overvoltages in high-voltage transmission and distribution systems (2 hours). Fundamentals of overvoltage theory. Types of overvoltages. Characteristics of temporary overvoltages in power systems. Causes of overvoltages with gentle, steep, and very steep fronts. Phenomena affecting the waveforms and peak values of overvoltages stressing insulation systems of electrical devices. Characteristics of electrical stresses. Permissible levels of operational stresses. Influence of overvoltages on insulation systems of power devices.

Electrical strength of large air insulation clearances (2 hours). Earth and phase-to-phase insulation. Model systems of large insulation clearances. Electrical strength under switching, lightning, and alternating impulse voltage. Standardized insulation levels. Conditions for the development of electrical discharges.

Impulse strength of external insulation of transmission lines and power substations (2 hours). Impulse characteristic – determination methods. Application of impulse characteristic in insulation coordination. Mathematical models of impulse strength. Leader development method.

Applications of the Leader Development Method (LDM) in assessing overvoltage stresses in power systems (2 hours). Models of power system elements under the influence of atmospheric overvoltages and their implementations in the EMTP-ATP program. Phenomenon of backflashover. Analysis of overvoltage stresses in power substations due to lightning discharges to overhead transmission lines.

Statistical methods in electrical strength testing (2 hours). Conventional testing with withstand voltage and 100-percent voltage. Impulse voltage testing. Series method, Tetzner method, up-and-down method.

Control of electric field distribution in electrical equipment designs (2 hours). Theoretical foundations of electric field distribution control. Examples of control screens in electrical equipment designs. Internal and external screens. Surface control. Fundamentals of designing high-voltage insulation systems. Influence of control on the design of electrical equipment.

Operation of electrical equipment in high and extra-high voltage substations (2 hours). Requirements for the operating conditions of power equipment. Scope of work and tests carried out under operating conditions. Operating conditions of high-voltage insulation systems for overhead lines, cable lines, transformers, gas-insulated switchgear.

High-voltage power supply and control of electrostatic precipitator operation (2 hours). Principle of operation of electrostatic precipitators. Basic parameters and operating characteristics. Typical power supply systems for electrostatic precipitators. Selection of high-voltage power supply equipment. Special issues.

The role of voltage stresses in the design and operation of high-voltage power systems (2 hours). Effectiveness of grounding the power system. Significance of temporary overvoltages. Counteracting the ferroresonance phenomenon. Limiting the level of switching overvoltages. Overvoltage phenomena in gas insulation systems.

Fundamentals of overvoltage protection for power devices (2 hours). Methods of protecting electrical devices from lightning overvoltages. Ways to reduce overvoltages generated during switching operations. Methods of limiting temporary overvoltages in electrical networks. Basic surge arresters used in power systems.

High Voltage Direct Current (HVDC) transmission of electrical energy (2 hours). Purpose and scope of application of DC transmission systems. Typical DC transmission systems. Comparison of design solutions for AC and DC transmission lines and cables. Investment and operating costs. Characteristics of operating DC transmission systems.

Electromagnetic impact of power facilities (3 hours). Electromagnetic field in the vicinity of high-voltage transmission and distribution systems. Selected issues of environmental protection in the design and operation of high-voltage transmission and distribution systems. Characteristics of disturbing and dangerous interactions. Methods of limiting them. Standardization recommendations regarding the impact of devices on the environment.

Perspectives for the development of high-voltage electro-insulation systems (1 hour). Gas-insulated transmission lines (GIL), gas-insulated switchgear (GIS), hybrid cables. Development of devices with vacuum insulation systems. Multi-circuit overhead transmission lines. Development of composite overhead insulation systems.
Design of insulation systems for overhead transmission lines (2 hours).
Design of insulation systems for power cables (2 hours).
Design of fragments of insulation systems for equipment with sulfur hexafluoride (2 hours).
Design of bushing, post, and protective insulators for power equipment (2 hours).
Design of high-voltage impulse test generators (2 hours).
Design of standardized current impulse generators (2 hours).
Design of overvoltage protection for high-voltage equipment (2 hours).
Analog modeling of electric fields (3 hours).
Control of electric field distribution in insulation systems (3 hours).
Forms of electrical discharges in gas insulation systems. Influence of space charge on the mechanism of electrical discharges (4 hours).
Testing of voltage distribution on an insulator string (3 hours).
Electric field under high-voltage transmission lines (3 hours).
Magnetic field under high-voltage transmission lines (3 hours). Methods for limiting the magnetic field under high-voltage transmission lines.
Ferroresonance overvoltages in power systems (3 hours).
Switching overvoltages in power systems (3 hours).
Modeling of the shielding zone (3 hours).
assessment_rules: Lectures are verified by an exam. Laboratory classes are passed based on a test or project. Project classes are passed based on the execution of a project, a test, or a project. Passing the module requires passing all laboratory classes.
